headword: {勇気|ゆうき}を{振|ふ}り{絞|しぼ}る
gloss: to summon one's courage; to muster up courage

definitions.gloss: to summon one's courage; to muster up courage; to screw up one's courage
definitions.explanation: To gather all of one's courage to face something difficult or frightening. The verb {振|ふ}り{絞|しぼ}る literally means "to wring out," conveying the image of squeezing out every last drop of bravery.

examples.japanese: {勇気|ゆうき}を{振|ふ}り{絞|しぼ}って⟦{告白|こくはく}した→告白する：19631_kokuhakusuru⟧。
examples.english: I mustered up my courage and confessed my feelings.

examples.japanese: {勇気|ゆうき}を{振|ふ}り{絞|しぼ}って⟦{社長|しゃちょう}→社長：01428_shachou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{意見|いけん}→意見：01303_iken⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{言|い}った→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: I summoned my courage and spoke my mind to the company president.

examples.japanese: ⟦{怖|こわ}かった→怖い：00864_kowai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、{勇気|ゆうき}を{振|ふ}り{絞|しぼ}って⟦{暗|くら}い→暗い：00647_kurai⟧⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{一人|ひとり}→一人：00630_hitori⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{歩|ある}いた→歩く：00538_aruku⟧。
examples.english: I was scared, but I mustered my courage and walked the dark road alone.

notes:
USAGE:
A set expression using the verb ⟦{振|ふ}り{絞|しぼ}る→振り絞る：12817_furishiboru⟧ (to wring out, to squeeze out). The image is of squeezing out the last drops of courage from within oneself. Typically used when facing a frightening, embarrassing, or challenging situation.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {勇気|ゆうき}を{振|ふ}り{絞|しぼ}って + action (mustering courage to do something)
- ⟦{最後|さいご}→最後：01413_saigo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{勇気|ゆうき}を{振|ふ}り{絞|しぼ}る (to summon one's last ounce of courage)

SIMILAR WORDS:
⟦{勇気|ゆうき}→勇気：02499_yuuki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧ (to show courage) is simpler and less dramatic. ⟦{振|ふ}り{絞|しぼ}る→振り絞る：12817_furishiboru⟧ adds the nuance of a supreme effort to overcome fear.
